name: Modern SEO M1 L2: Live website breakdown
body:
> Module 1, about 10 minutes of lesson (player shows 10:09) recorded in 4 parts totaling 17:01. Source: Lesson 2 Live website breakdown.mp4 (5:37), Lesson 2 continuation_1.mp4 (1:14), Lesson 2 continuation_2.mp4 (4:02), Lesson 2 continuation_3.mp4 (6:08)

> Timestamp key: **P1** = Live website breakdown, **P2** = continuation_1, **P3** = continuation_2, **P4** = continuation_3. Each part's clock starts at 0:00. P2 repeats the end of P1, and P3 starts by repeating the end of P2. See Open questions.

## In short
- The demo diagnoses a real "stuck" business: Kelley & Dawson Service, an HVAC company in Wichita, Kansas, for the keyword "air conditioning repair Wichita."
- Start by sizing up the top 3 map results: run a `site:` search on each domain to count indexed pages. That gives a rough content target.
- Pick an audit target with lots of reviews, weak rankings, and a primary category that matches the keyword. Reviews are harder to fix than GBP and website basics.
- Four quick fixes the instructor says take about half an hour: title tag, H1, LocalBusiness schema, and more GBP services. Then Core 30 content to match competitors' site size.
- Prospecting angle: offer to make the quick fixes for free, since proving a fast ranking gain builds long-term trust.

## Key ideas
- **Primary category follows what people search.** For HVAC, most work comes from broken AC, so people search "air conditioning repair." The instructor says that is "almost always the primary category we target for HVAC contractors," not "HVAC contractor" or "air conditioning replacement." (P1 1:07)
- **Indexed page count as a size benchmark.** A `site:domain.com` search shows roughly how many pages Google has indexed. The Wichita top 3 had 39, 62, and 134. From that he guessed 60 to 90 pages to compete, while noting one site ranks with only 39. (P1 2:15)
- **Choosing a target.** Look in "More businesses" for a business with many reviews, poor ranking, and a primary category matching the keyword. Skip ones that muddy the analysis: On Time Plumbing, Heating, Cooling has about 3.9K reviews but "plumbing" in its name, and Bryan's Heating & Air (807 reviews) is in Valley Center, too far from Wichita. (P1 3:17, P2 0:38)
- **Grid range matters.** The first rank map used a very wide grid (25,577 m between points) and showed 0% top 3. Rerun at a tighter range (2,504 m), it showed top 3 results around the business address. Not ranking top 3 at your own GBP address is "usually a pretty bad sign." (P3 0:34 to 1:42)
- **Compare Top 3% against competitors.** Sorting competitors by Top 3% showed several in the "30, 25, 20, 18 range" against Kelley & Dawson's 8.28%. That gap is the room to grow. (P3 1:54)
- **Do not change a primary category that is working.** He was "tempted" to switch the primary from Air conditioning contractor to Air conditioning repair service but would not, because they rank well enough. (P3 2:33, P4 0:54)
- **Website and GBP must match.** Title tag and H1 should contain the primary category and city name. Phone should match the GBP and be click-to-call. The page should embed the GBP and show reviews. Schema should include LocalBusiness and services.
- **GBP activity does not replace basics.** Kelley & Dawson posts on GBP and has many photos and reviews, but "a lot of the basics just aren't done correctly." (P4 1:39)
- **Free quick wins as a sales tool.** "When you demonstrate that you can improve their ranking very quickly with minimal effort, then they're much more likely to trust you over the long term." (P4 2:04)

## Step-by-step process
The diagnostic, in the instructor's order:
1. Search the main money keyword plus city in Google (shown: "air conditioning repair wichita ks"). For HVAC, use "air conditioning repair." (P1 1:07)
2. Open the top 3 businesses in the map pack (Dan's Heating and Cooling, Air Source Heating & Air Conditioning, Moody Heating & Air Conditioning). (P1 1:40)
3. For each, copy the website domain and search `site:` plus the domain. Note the result count as indexed pages (39, 62, 134). (P1 2:01)
4. Estimate the content size needed to compete (his blind guess: 60 to 90 pages). (P1 2:34)
5. Click "More businesses" and choose a target outside the top 3: many reviews, poor ranking, primary category matching the keyword, close to the city. Skip businesses with off-topic names or far-away addresses. (P1 3:04, P2 0:02 to 0:38)
6. Run `site:` on the target's domain (Kelley & Dawson: 10 results, "light on content"). (P3 0:13)
7. Run a grid rank map for "primary keyword + city" (shown in LeadSnap). If the wide grid shows nothing, rerun at a tighter range. Check whether they are top 3 at their own address. (P3 0:34 to 1:42)
8. Sort competitors by Top 3% to see how much room there is to grow. (P3 1:54)
9. Use GMB Everywhere's Category Finder and audit to pull the GBP data (categories, services). (P3 2:10)
10. Check the primary category against the keyword. Change it only if it is clearly wrong and rankings are poor. (P3 2:33)
11. Count GBP services. Kelley & Dawson had 7 or 8. He wants 20 to 30. (P3 2:47)
12. Check the homepage title tag and H1 for primary category plus city name. (P3 2:58 to 3:39)
13. Check the phone number: is it click-to-call, and does it match the GBP? (P3 3:40)
14. Scroll the homepage: are reviews showing, is there a GBP embed, are affiliations linked out? (P4 0:02 to 0:21)
15. Test structured data with a schema validator (shown: validator.schema.org). Look for LocalBusiness schema and service schema. (P4 0:23 to 0:45)
16. Review the GBP itself: overview matches the site, review count, recent posts, photos. (P4 1:17 to 1:55)
17. List the quick fixes, then plan Core 30 content to close the site-size gap with the top 3. (P4 0:45 to 1:14)
18. When prospecting, offer to make the quick fixes for free. (P4 1:57)

## Checklist
- Search the primary keyword plus city and note the top 3 map results.
- Run `site:` on each top 3 domain and record indexed page counts.
- Run `site:` on the client domain and compare.
- Run a rank map for primary category + city. Use a tight enough grid to see the area around the address.
- Confirm whether the business ranks top 3 at its own GBP address.
- Sort competitors by Top 3% and note the gap.
- Primary category matches what customers actually search (do not change it if rankings are already good).
- GBP lists 20 to 30 services (not 7 or 8).
- Homepage title tag includes primary category + city name.
- Homepage H1 includes primary category + city name.
- Phone number is click-to-call and matches the GBP exactly.
- Reviews widget actually displays reviews.
- GBP map is embedded on the page.
- Affiliation logos link out to the organizations.
- LocalBusiness schema is present, plus schema for each service.
- GBP overview details match the website.
- GBP posts and photos are active (good, but not a substitute for the basics).

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Google search, `site:` operator | Count a domain's indexed pages | P1 2:01, P3 0:13 |
| Google "More businesses" (local finder) | See map rankings beyond the top 3 and pick an audit target | P1 3:04 |
| LeadSnap (app.leadsnap.com) Heat Map | Grid rank map: avg rank, Top 3%, market share, competitor table, keyword volume and CPC | P3 0:34 to 1:54 |
| GMB Everywhere (Chrome extension) | Category Finder, quick GBP audit, and Services view; adds buttons (Basic, AI, Teleport, Review, Post, Local Scan) to search results | P3 2:10 |
| Structured data testing tool (shown: validator.schema.org, Schema Markup Validator) | Check which schema types a page has | P4 0:28 |
| Core 30 | Content production to match competitor site size and build topical relevance | P3 0:25, P4 1:07 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
These are the instructor's claims or what was shown on screen, not verified facts.
- Top 3 indexed pages for the Wichita search: Dan's 39 (danshc.com, shown), Air Source 62 (audio only), Moody 134 (shown). (P1 2:18 to 2:30)
- Estimated pages needed to compete in this market: 60 to 90. (P1 2:43)
- Kelley & Dawson indexed pages: 10. Suggested addition: "maybe 20 or 30 pages with the Core 30." (P3 0:19 to 0:25)
- Kelley & Dawson GBP on screen: 5.0 stars, 541 reviews, 65+ years in business, open 24 hours, 1741 N Broadway St, Wichita, KS 67214, (316) 263-7201. (P1 3:25 frame, P3 0:45 frame)
- On Time Plumbing, Heating, Cooling: about 3.9K reviews ("4,000" in audio), Bel Aire, KS. (P1 3:48, P1 4:05 frame)
- Bryan's Heating & Air Conditioning: 807 reviews, Valley Center, KS. (P2 0:38, P2 0:25 frame)
- LeadSnap wide grid (13 x 13, 169 points, 25,577 m apart, Sep 26, 2025): avg ranking 19.10, Top 3% 0%, market share 0.00%. (P3 0:45 frame)
- LeadSnap tighter grid (13 x 13, 2,504 m apart, area 897.99 km²): avg ranking 11.35 (5th), Top 3% 8.28% (13th), market share 24.55% (13th). (P3 1:45 frame)
- Keyword "air conditioning repair wichita" in LeadSnap: difficulty 23, search volume 110, CPC $46.14. (P3 0:45 frame)
- Competitor Top 3% on the tighter grid: Air Source 33.73%, Mike's & Sappio's 26.04%, Fahnestock Plumbing 24.26%, On Time Plumbing 20.12%, Bryan's 18.34%, Reddi 16.57%, Rods Cooling 15.38%. (P3 2:05 frame) The instructor summarized this as "30, 25, 20, 18." (P3 1:54)
- GBP services: Kelley & Dawson has "seven, eight." Target: 20 to 30. (P3 2:47)
- The four core fixes can be done "in a half hour." (P4 1:04)

## Terms
**Primary category:** The main GBP category. Should match what customers actually search for the main service.
**`site:` search:** Google search of `site:domain.com` that lists the pages Google has indexed for that domain.
**Rank map / heat map:** A grid of points around the business showing its map ranking at each point for one keyword.
**Top 3%:** Share of rank map grid points where the business is in the top 3. (Whisper wrote it as "top 3%" at P3 0:40, which is this metric.)
**GBP embed:** A Google Map of the business profile embedded on the website.
**LocalBusiness schema:** Structured data telling Google the page belongs to a local business. Kelley & Dawson only had WebPage schema.
**Click-to-call:** A phone number linked so tapping it starts a call.

## Worth quoting
- "Getting lots of reviews is usually more difficult than basic optimization of their GBP and website." (P1 3:39)
- "We want the primary category and city name in the title tag." (P3 3:09)
- "You could change those four things in a half hour." (P4 1:04)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Run this diagnostic on each client.** For Pipeliners, Alphalete, and Summit AZ: search the main service + city, `site:` the top 3 and the client, and compare page counts. This gives a quick content gap number before any Core 30 planning.
- **Homepage (GBP landing page) checks.** Recommendations for Kim to verify and apply: title tag and H1 contain primary category + city, click-to-call phone, GBP embed, working reviews display, LocalBusiness plus service schema. Client sites are read-only for Claude, so any fix goes to Kim as a copy-paste list.
- **Phone match on Summit AZ.** The lesson checks that the site phone matches the GBP. Summit AZ uses GHL call tracking that swaps the displayed number in the browser, while the real number (480) 447-7008 stays in the HTML and schema (source: memory file `feedback_summit_ghl_dni.md`). When Kim runs this check on Summit, compare the HTML/schema number, not a browser screenshot, and leave the tracking snippet alone.
- **GBP services count.** Have Kim count each client's GBP services against the instructor's 20 to 30 target, adding only services the client really offers.
- **Primary category.** Check each client's primary category against what customers search, but follow the rule from this lesson: if they already rank well, leave it.
- **Rank maps.** The instructor uses LeadSnap, which is a paid tool. Do not sign up without Kim's approval (memory file `feedback_no_paid_services.md`). Check first whether a tool TAG already pays for can produce a grid rank map.

## Open questions
- **Overlapping recordings.** P1 3:13 to 3:58 and P2 0:02 to 0:49 cover the same segment (choosing the target). P3 0:01 to 0:12 repeats the end of P2. Content was merged once in these notes.
- **Dead air.** P1 has no speech after about 3:58 (frames to 5:25 show a static map). P4 has no speech after about 2:20 (frames to 5:45 show a static rank map, then a black screen at 6:05). Nothing seems to be missing, but Kim may want to confirm the original lesson ends with the Kelley & Dawson wrap-up.
- **Transcript glitch.** P1 1:46 to 1:54 repeats a phrase ("We have Dan's repair is typically the desired primary category"). Looks like a recording or transcription repeat, not new content.
- **Name corrections from screen:** "Kelly" and "Kelly and Dawson" = Kelley & Dawson Service. "Felix" = Fenix Heating & Cooling (417 reviews, on screen at P2 0:25). "Brian" = Bryan's Heating & Air Conditioning. "AirSource" = Air Source Heating & Air Conditioning. "Tim in Wichita" at P3 0:01 is likely a cut-off "...him in Wichita" (unclear in video).
- **Air Source's 62 pages** was said but not seen in any frame.
- **Primary category wording.** In P1 he says target "air conditioning repair." On the GBP he says "air conditioning repair service." GMB Everywhere shows Kelley & Dawson already has "Air conditioning repair service" as a secondary category. The note "I'd be tempted to replace" implies swapping which one is primary.
- **"Overview, we'd wanna make sure that matched"** (P4 1:20): he does not say what must match. Likely NAP details against the website (unclear in video).
- **Instructor identity.** The LeadSnap account on screen is logged in as "Caleb Ulku." This may be the instructor (unclear in video).
- **The H1.** The homepage hero heading shown is "Wichita's Heating and Cooling Experts." The instructor calls it the H1 but no page source was shown to confirm.
- The 60 to 90 page estimate is a "completely blind" guess by the instructor, not a rule.
- No low-confidence transcript lines in any part.

## Timestamps

- P1 0:38 How he looks at a prospect's website and competition

- P1 1:40 Open the top 3 map results

- P1 2:34 Estimate: 60 to 90 pages to compete
- P1 2:57 "More businesses": choosing an audit target
- P1 3:39 Reviews are harder than basic GBP and website fixes
- P1 3:48 Skipping On Time Plumbing (plumbing in name)
- P2 0:38 Skipping Bryan's (too far from Wichita); choosing Kelley & Dawson
- P3 0:13 Kelley & Dawson `site:` search: 10 results
- P3 0:34 LeadSnap rank map: wide grid shows 0% top 3
- P3 0:57 Rerunning the rank map at a tighter range
- P3 1:42 Tighter map: top 3 around the address; competitor Top 3% comparison
- P3 2:10 GMB Everywhere Category Finder and services
- P3 2:33 Primary category: tempted to change, but would not
- P3 2:47 Services: 7 or 8, want 20 to 30
- P3 2:58 Title tag and H1 missing primary category and city
- P3 3:40 Phone not click-to-call; number matches GBP
- P4 0:02 Broken reviews embed, affiliations should link out, no GBP embed
- P4 0:23 Schema check: only WebPage schema

- P4 1:55 Offer the fixes for free to win trust
